chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the performer of exclusive Hajj (Mufrid) who brings forward his Tawaf, or delays it? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, it is the same, whether he hastens it or delays it.'

key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: The performer of exclusive Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrid)

ai.seo_question: Can a Mufrid delay their first Tawaf of Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility for the Mufrid regarding the timing of the Tawaf al-Qudum, affirming that neither accelerating nor delaying the ritual carries legal disadvantage. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (yusr) in Hajj rituals, distinguishing the Mufrid's practice from the Tamattu' where specific sequencing is often emphasized. The hadith serves as a foundational text for fiqh discussions on the validity of Hajj rites when performed out of the 'ideal' chronological order.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the performer of exclusive Hajj bringing forward his Tawaaf, or should he delay it?’ So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj, it is the same, hastening it or delaying it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for Mufrid al-Hajj; if he can perform his Tawaf first or later. He (the Imam) said, Tt, by Allah, is the same to perform immediately or later.’”
